title: Cocktail 2 Opens Big. Fourteen Years On, the Diaspora's Favourite Love Triangle Is Pouring Again.
excerpt: Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika's spiritual successor lands a four-star verdict, 100K+ advance tickets and an 8.83 cr start — proving there's still an audience for a love story with no superheroes attached.
body:
Fourteen years ago, a backless dress, a Goan sunset, and three people who didn't know who they were in love with rewrote the rulebook for the Hindi rom-com. **Cocktail** (2012) was modest on paper — a 35 crore budget — and seismic in the culture, grossing over 121 crore worldwide and minting a soundtrack that still owns wedding dance floors. So when **Cocktail 2** finally poured into theatres this Friday, June 19, it wasn't just another release. It was a sequel carrying a legacy in one hand and a 2026 box office that no longer plays by 2012's rules in the other.

<youtube></youtube>

Early signs say the gamble is paying off. The **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, and **Rashmika Mandanna** starrer opened to a healthy 8.83 crore advance gross — block seats included — and within hours had crossed the 100,000-ticket mark on BookMyShow, becoming only the fourth Hindi film of 2026 to hit a six-figure advance. The company it keeps is telling: the record-shredding *Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge*, the war drama *Border 2*, and the horror-comedy *Bhooth Bangla*. For a song-and-dance romance with no explosions to sell, that's a flex.

> "#Cocktail2: WINNER. More than lives up to expectations... Solid performances, superb music, stunning visuals, and captivating writing — this film scores on all fronts." — Taran Adarsh

That four-star verdict from the trade's most-watched reviewer landed the night before release, and the momentum followed. BookMyShow sales surged from a sleepy 6,950 on June 14 to a roaring 69,720 on June 18 — the kind of last-48-hours spike that signals genuine want, not manufactured hype. By the afternoon shows on day one, the film had crossed 2.25 crore net across more than 4,160 screens, with the all-important evening and night window still to come. Trade projections peg the opening between 11 and 12 crore — which, if it holds, makes this Kriti Sanon's second-biggest post-pandemic opener, leapfrogging *Crew*.

For **Shahid Kapoor**, the stakes are personal. His February outing *O Romeo* was a commercial flat note, netting just 8.50 crore on day one despite a wide release. Cocktail 2 has already cleared that bar in advances alone. He returns here looking every bit the matured romantic lead — sharper, more lived-in — and slots into the kind of role that built his reputation in the first place. The chemistry experiment this time pits Sanon and Mandanna as the two poles of the love triangle, and the early word is that the casting alone is doing half the seductive heavy lifting.


Director **Homi Adajania** is back in the chair, and that continuity matters. The original's appeal was never just the glamour — it was the way Adajania let messy, modern people be selfish and sympathetic at once. The sequel keeps his signature visual sheen: glossy locations, a wardrobe that belongs on a mood board, and a **Pritam**-led soundtrack ("Mashooqa," the Arijit Singh–Sunidhi Chauhan duet "Tujhko") engineered to outlive the film's theatrical run. The CBFC handed it an A certificate, a nod to the grown-up tone — this is a rom-com for adults who've had their hearts broken at least once.

**For the diaspora**, Cocktail 2 is a theatrical event before it's a stream. The film opened worldwide on June 19, with advance bookings live across North American and UK multiplex chains catering to the desi audience — expect screenings at the usual AMC, Cinemark, and Cineworld locations that carry Hindi releases. There's no streaming date confirmed yet; if the original's playbook holds, a digital premiere will follow several weeks after the theatrical window, most likely on a major OTT platform. For now, this is one to catch on the big screen, where Adajania's frames are meant to be seen.

The larger story is what this Friday kicks off. Cocktail 2 is the opening salvo in Bollywood's most crowded summer window in years — *Alpha*, *Welcome to the Jungle*, and a parade of July releases are stacked right behind it. Whether the industry can convert a strong start into a genuine hit-making season depends partly on films exactly like this one: mid-budget, star-led, built on charm rather than spectacle. If the romance lands and the music sticks, Cocktail 2 won't just honour its predecessor — it'll prove there's still an audience that turns up for a love story, no superheroes required.

The first sip looks promising. Now we find out if the buzz lasts past the weekend.
